facts.text: The README describes the package as an unofficial Python library for remote-controlling the Temi robot via WebSocket
A Temi-side Android application creates a WebSocket server at ws://TEMI_IP:8175 and waits for connections from the Python API
The client is constructed with the WebSocket URI of the Temi server: Temi(uri)
connect() retries with a default of 3 tries and 5 s between tries, then raises
Every command is a JSON object with a command name and a generated UUID id, and the reply must carry the same id
command() sends the JSON over a new WebSocket connection and waits for a reply with the same id
The speak command takes a sentence and is answered with the id only
The ask command speaks a sentence and answers with the recognized reply in an answer field
The goto command names a saved location and answers with success true when Temi reached it and false otherwise
The API format documents raise_head with an angle field
The README lists turn by an angle and states no unit or range for it
The README states a screen tilt range of -25 to 55, gives no unit and then shows a turn call
The README says every command supports a timeout and that a goto which timed out may keep walking, after which the caller can command Temi to stop
The example opens a URL with interface(url=...)
run() gathers the tasks queued by the command templates
disconnect() closes the socket if it is still open

safe_state.description: Temi has been sent the stop command; the runtime latch refuses further commands until an operator reset
